reviews.comment: Exams were made so difficult that over 30 people have to retake the class, so much so that they added 205 to take the semester after so everyone can still stay on track (this is not typical).

Chen 204 is a tough class. Everyone knows this. Dr. Sun knows this too, and does her best to make it more manageable. Gave various extra credit assignments for all exams worth 10-20 bonus points, from solving new problems during recitation or redoing incorrect exam problems. Clear lectures, very accessible by email/office hours for HW/questions.

Dr Sun was a great 204 prof. This class is tough, you can find online that it is the hardest sophomore year CHEN course. Whatever you do, take Dr. J or Rui Sun. Do not, I repeat, do not take mashuga. The stories that come out of that are insane. Even then, doesn't matter which prof you take, its going to be hard no matter what.

Professor Sun is very caring, however, her class is not easy. My best advice it to take advantage of the textbook and do every extra credit assignment. She does not end up curving the class at the end.

She was an ok professor, her lectures were ok and she goes through the material pretty well. Try to keep up with the material and don't get behind. She'll give extra credit but it's all or nothing so it's pretty difficult to get which makes me doubt if she really cares about her students.

204 is just difficult in general. Sun gives very clear and laid out lectures that are extremely helpful. I recommend reading the textbook before content is covered in class. Overall tip is if you don't understand what class was about, understand it before the next class. Sun clearly cares about her students and works to give second chances

reviews.comment: CHEN 204 is tough, but Dr. Sun truly makes it worth taking. She explains concepts clearly, goes in depth, and genuinely cares about her students. Her office hours are incredibly helpful, the homework prepares you well, and even though the tests are challenging, she gives lots of practice and grades generously with extra credit opportunities.
